transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Iggy Park (LumenPay SRE), Dana Chu (LumenPay Head of Security), Priya Rao (Eng Manager), Tom Becker (Product), Hannah Li (Compliance)

Summary: quick post-incident retro focused on KV cache fallback that caused elevated latency and partial degradation for payment reconciliation calls; regulatory readout on audit logs and data egress expectations.

Topics: incident timeline, root cause hypothesis (KV cache eviction cascade + config drift), mitigation done (short-term rollback, rate limiter change, canary of dedicated pool), long-term fixes (prefix sharding, tougher telemetry), compliance requirements (audit schema, retention), next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. We know this is a packed week so we'll aim to keep it tight. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Iggy (LumenPay): Hi Iggy here.
[00:10] Dana (LumenPay): Dana, hi.
[00:12] Priya (LumenPay): Priya.
[00:14] Tom (LumenPay): Tom.
[00:16] Hannah (LumenPay): Hannah.
[00:18] Connor (Redwood SE): Connor here.
[00:20] Sofia (Redwood CSM): Sofia.
[00:22] Maya: Awesome, thanks. We'll run through a short timeline, then Connor will walk the technical hypothesis, then we do compliance readout and agree owners.

[02:05] Connor (Redwood SE): Okay timeline: on 2027-04-12 around 03:12 UTC LumenPay saw increased 95th and 99th p50 sorry p95 latency for the reconciliation endpoint. There was elevated token generation times, and downstream you saw request backpressure causing queues to pile. Our alerting detected model errors and timeouts and auto-fallback triggered but the fallback to smaller model had higher per-request overhead because of serialization churn.
[02:40] Priya: Quick clarification - the fallback you mention, was that the hosted -> dedicated fallback or model size fallback? I think we configured both.
[02:48] Connor: Right so there were two fallbacks engaged: first the smart routing moved traffic from your hosted pool to the dedicated pool, and then within the dedicated pool the runtime fell back from the quantized 4bit model to an FP16 variant due to kernel mismatch on that GPU family. The FP16 path had longer generation latency because of memory thrash.
[03:10] Iggy: And we saw KV cache miss rates spike at the same time, is that correlated?
[03:15] Connor: Yes. Our replay shows a KV cache eviction cascade: long-tailed prefixes from your reconciliation workload caused the KV cache to thrash, increased recompute, and then more tokens were requested creating a positive feedback loop.
[03:27] Tom: Sorry, can you say "K V" cache again? The transcriber says V P C earlier and it's confusing.
[03:33] Maya: Yeah we sometimes see V P C get mangled. It's KV cache, key-value cache for transformer states.

[05:00] Dana (LumenPay): From security/compliance, the big ask is auditability of the fallback decisions and egress logs. During the incident we needed to show whether data left our VPC and which model variants saw PII.
[05:18] Sofia (Redwood CSM): Noted. We have an anonymized egress log extract we can share, and Connor will add trace IDs matched to fallbacks.
[05:28] Hannah (LumenPay): We also need retention policy alignment — 7 years is our default for payment logs, but we know your hosted tier has shorter retention.
[05:36] Maya: Correct, hosted default is 90 days for traces. For Private or Dedicated we can extend retention, and for your requirements we'd recommend Redwood Private or a dedicated archive integration to your S3. We'll include the retention options in the doc.

[07:45] Connor: Technical hypothesis detail: the primary root cause is config drift in your batching window + the KV cache shard configuration. A recent deploy (customer side) changed prefixing behavior which increased distinct cache keys by ~7x for reconciliation. The cache's LRU then evicted older contexts, which increased recompute. Also, kernel selection heuristics on a small fraction of GPUs picked an FP16 kernel incompatible with the quantized path, forcing path backoff.
[08:20] Priya: That deploy changed a header we use to partition by tenant, didn't anticipate it would alter the key derivation for model prefixes. We own that change — we missed the test.
[08:30] Connor: Totally understandable — it's one of those subtle interactions. In our post-incident replay we saw a pattern: threshold crossing at about 500 concurrent reconciliation streams per worker caused the eviction cascade.

[10:10] Iggy: Walk me through what you changed to mitigate in the hotfix window.
[10:15] Connor: Short-term we did three things: 1) rate-limited reconciliation to 350 concurrency per worker (config in canary), 2) disabled the aggressive KV LRU compaction for your tenant only, and 3) pinned kernel selection to the quantized path for the affected GPUs. That restored latencies to baseline within ~12 minutes.
[10:42] Tom: That pinning step — any risk moving forward? Like do we lose an optimization?
[10:48] Connor: There's minor throughput loss on some workloads, about 4-6% CPU/GPU efficiency, but it's safe. Long-term we want to do smarter prefix sharding so the LRU doesn't collide.

[12:00] Hannah: For the regulatory readout, we need an export of every decision point — when the fallback triggered, the reason code, and the trace id mapping. Also a certificate that no raw payment data left the customer VPC during the incident.
[12:18] Maya: We'll provide the decision timeline CSV and a signed statement from Redwood engineering about our egress controls. Connor, can you attach the trace mapping?
[12:26] Connor: Yep I have that as an anonymized mapping file; will scrub PII. We'll include trace ids and fallback reason codes.

[15:00] Priya: On the long-term fix, you mentioned prefix sharding and telemetry. What does that roadmap look like?
[15:06] Connor: Roadmap: 1) prefix-aware sharding - modify the runtime so keys are bucketed by stable prefix hash (ETA 6 weeks), 2) improved kernel selection telemetry and fallback policy (ETA 3 weeks for release candidate), 3) configurable tenant-level KV limits exposed in console (ETA 4 weeks). We'll prioritize LumenPay for the prefix sharding work and schedule dedicated cluster benchmarks.
[15:34] Dana: Important for us: can we request a regulatory-friendly lane where audit logs are immutable and retention is customer controlled? We can't rely on short retention windows.
[15:44] Maya: Yes, that's a standard ask. For Redwood Private we provide customer-managed S3 + object lock options. We'll document the steps and costs.

[18:50] Iggy: A few gotchas we saw in our internal postmortem: the alert thresholds were too coarse, and our runbook didn't include the right internal trace tags, so we spent 14 minutes searching for correlation. We'll add the specific trace fields in the ticket.
[19:06] Sofia: We'll review your runbook with you and suggest additional alerting templates — we've got a playbook for KV-cache symptoms.

[21:40] Tom: On costs — there's been talk internally about switching more traffic to hosted during peaks to save ops cost. But if hosted has shorter retention and weaker auditability, that won't fly with compliance. What's the cost delta if we keep dedicated but add extended logs?
[21:58] Maya: We'll send a pricing delta: dedicated baseline + extended retention addon plus S3 archive. I'll include a few scenarios (monthly token volume ranges). We'll make it explicit per-GB storage and per-query retrieval cost.

[25:10] Connor: One more technical note — we found a small bug in the prefix hash when tenant IDs are numeric-only (leading zeros were dropped by a middleware). That explains why only a subset of your tenants hit the cascade. Fix is trivial and we'll patch in next 48 hours.
[25:30] Priya: Yep that's consistent. Our reconciliation runs have some legacy tenant IDs.

[28:00] Dana: We need to ensure SSO/SAML access to audit logs for our auditors. Also, RBAC must prevent broad access within our org.
[28:12] Sofia: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. We'll include the SSO metadata and recommended roles for auditors.

[31:50] Hannah: For the compliance package, we'll need: 1) SOC2 summary, 2) signed egress statement, 3) retention options and proof of immutability, 4) trace mapping for the incident.
[32:04] Maya: We'll bundle that and send as a single package.

[34:20] Connor: Operational follow-up: I propose a KV cache benchmark run on a dedicated cluster using your production replay, and then a second test with the prefix sharding patch applied. This will quantify the perf delta and inform the rollout policy. Can LumenPay provide a sanitized request replay?
[34:38] Iggy: Yes we can provide a sanitized replay of the reconciliation window. We'll scrub PII but keep prefixes and timing.

[36:10] Priya: Regarding canarying future releases — we want more guardrails in place so that a deploy that changes key derivation can't be rolled out globally without a throttled ramp and a safety switch.
[36:22] Connor: Agreed. We can add a deploy gating rule for schema-affecting changes and offer a console toggle for immediate tenant-level rate-limit.

[40:00] Tom: Any asks from your side to help us move faster?
[40:05] Connor: If you can prioritize the sanitized replay and the specific tenant IDs that saw the spike, we'll get the benchmark scheduled. Also a copy of the deploy diff that touched the prefix header would help root cause verification.
[40:20] Priya: We'll attach both to the Jira ticket.

[45:00] Dana: Quick legal/compliance question — will the signed egress statement expose Redwood internal configs or will it be a high-level summary? We need enough detail for auditors but not internal IP.
[45:12] Maya: We will provide a statement that includes the audit facts (what logs were captured, retention windows, who had access) and a redacted technical appendix. Legal and compliance at Redwood will sign.

[48:30] Sofia: Recap of action items and owners (quick): Maya will send compliance package; Connor will run KV replay and share perf; Priya/Iggy will share replay and deploy diff; Dana/Hannah will provide audit fields and retention requirements.
[48:52] Tom: Are we scheduling a follow-up in two weeks to check the benchmark results?
[48:57] Maya: Yes propose 2027-05-02, same time. We'll send an invite.

[50:15] Iggy: Two last quick clarifications: 1) When you say "prefix sharding" does that require migration downtime? 2) What does the canary look like?
[50:25] Connor: 1) No migration downtime expected; we do a rolling config and the cache buckets are additive. 2) Canary will be tenant-level with a 2% traffic ramp for 24 hours, auto-rollback on p95 regressions.
[50:40] Priya: Sounds good.

[55:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and the invite for 2027-05-02. If anything urgent, ping me or Connor.
[55:10] Dana: Thanks all.
[55:15] Hannah: Thanks.

[end]
